outputs.L1: The present invention provides a line-of-sight operation apparatus, a method, and a medical device that make it possible to appropriately determine whether movement of a user’s line of sight is intentional, while preventing the user from being subjected to an undue burden. The line-of-sight operation apparatus includes a display screen; a display control unit configured to display, on the display screen, an icon including an animation image; a line-of-sight detection unit configured to detect a line of sight of a user; a following determination unit configured to determine, based on a result of detection performed by the line-of-sight detection unit, whether movement of the user’s line of sight follows movement of the animation image; and an output unit configured to output information indicating that the icon has been selected when the following determination unit determines that the movement of the user’s line of sight follows the movement of the animation image.
outputs.L2: The invention relates to a gaze-based operating apparatus, an associated method, and a medical device that can suitably judge whether a user’s eye movement is intentional while avoiding imposing an unnecessary burden on the user. The gaze operation apparatus is provided with a display screen; a display controller that presents, on the display screen, an icon containing an animated image; a gaze detector that detects the user’s line of sight; a tracking judgment unit that, using the detection result obtained by the gaze detector, decides whether the user’s gaze movement is tracking the motion of the animated image; and an output unit that, when the tracking judgment unit determines that the user’s gaze movement corresponds to the animated image’s motion, outputs information showing that the icon has been selected.
outputs.L3:
The invention provides a line-of-sight operation apparatus, a line-of-sight operation method, and a medical device capable of determining whether movement of a user’s gaze is intentional. In particular, the invention is useful for systems in which a user performs an operation by looking at a specific target on a display screen.

In conventional gaze-based operation systems, it may be difficult to distinguish between an intentional gaze movement made for the purpose of selecting an item and an unintentional gaze movement caused by ordinary visual behavior. As a result, a user may be required to maintain their gaze on an icon for a long time, repeat an operation, or perform an additional confirmation action. This can place a burden on the user, especially in medical environments or other situations where quick and reliable operation is required.

To address this issue, the line-of-sight operation apparatus includes a display screen and a display control unit. The display control unit displays an icon on the display screen together with an animation image. The animation image is configured to move in a predetermined manner, for example by changing position, shape, direction, or appearance over time. By presenting such movement, the apparatus provides the user with a visual cue that can be followed intentionally.

The apparatus further includes a line-of-sight detection unit that detects movement of the user’s line of sight. The line-of-sight detection unit monitors the user’s gaze while the animation image is being displayed and determines whether the detected gaze movement corresponds to, or follows, the movement of the animation image associated with the icon.

When the user’s line of sight follows the movement of the animation image, an output unit outputs information indicating that the icon has been selected. In this way, selection of the icon is based not merely on the user looking at a fixed position, but on the user intentionally tracking the displayed animation. This makes it possible to more accurately determine that the user intended to select the icon.

Accordingly, the invention reduces erroneous selections caused by accidental gaze movement and helps prevent the user from being burdened during gaze-based operation. The invention can be applied to various devices, including medical devices, in which reliable hands-free operation through line-of-sight input is desirable.
outputs.L4:
The invention relates to a technique for enabling a user to select an icon displayed on a screen without using the hands. In particular, the invention provides a user interface in which an icon displayed on a display device is animated in a predetermined manner, the user’s line of sight is detected, and it is determined whether movement of the user’s gaze corresponds to the movement of the animated icon.

In conventional line-of-sight input systems, an icon or other object may be selected when the user simply looks at it for a predetermined period of time. However, such systems can cause unintended selections, because a user may naturally look at an icon merely to read or observe it. In addition, requiring the user to stare at a fixed point for a long time can increase physical and mental burden. The present invention addresses these issues by requiring not only that the user look toward the icon, but also that the user’s gaze movement follow the animation of the icon.

According to the invention, a display control unit causes an icon to be displayed on a display screen and animates the icon according to a predetermined movement pattern. The animation may include, for example, movement of the icon in a horizontal, vertical, circular, oscillating, or otherwise recognizable path. A line-of-sight detection unit detects the direction of the user’s gaze and obtains gaze position information indicating where on the display the user is looking. A determination unit then compares the detected gaze movement with the animation pattern of the icon.

If the determination unit determines that the user’s line of sight follows the animated movement of the icon, the system recognizes this as an intentional selection operation. In response, an output unit outputs information indicating that the icon has been selected. This output may be used to execute a function associated with the icon, open an application, confirm a menu item, operate equipment, or perform another predetermined process.

Because selection is based on whether the gaze follows the icon’s animation, accidental selection caused by merely looking at the icon can be reduced. At the same time, the user is not required to perform a manual operation such as pressing a button, touching a screen, or using a mouse. The invention therefore enables reliable hands-free icon selection and improves the operability of devices for users who are unable to use their hands, users engaged in other tasks, or users operating equipment in environments where touch input is undesirable.

The system may further improve reliability by determining whether the gaze movement follows the animation for at least a predetermined time, whether the degree of correspondence between the gaze path and the icon movement exceeds a threshold, or whether the timing of the gaze movement matches the timing of the animation. The animation pattern may also be changed depending on the operating state, the type of icon, the user’s characteristics, or the required level of selection certainty. In this way, the invention provides an intuitive and intentional line-of-sight input method while reducing the burden placed on the user.

**The Power of “The”**

“The” is one of the smallest and most common words in the English language, yet it plays an important role in communication. It is called the definite article, and it helps us refer to a specific person, place, thing, or idea. For example, when we say “the book,” we usually mean a particular book that both the speaker and listener know about.

This simple word brings clarity and precision to sentences. Without “the,” English would often sound incomplete or confusing. It helps connect ideas, identify details, and make meaning more exact. Whether we are talking about “the sun,” “the world,” or “the future,” this tiny word gives importance and direction to what we say.

Although “the” may seem ordinary, it is essential. It shows that even the smallest words can have a powerful effect on language.

counterfactuals.prompt: Write a patent-style abstract for an eye-gaze controlled interface that selects an icon when the user’s line of sight follows an animated image on the display.
counterfactuals.output: An eye-gaze controlled user interface is provided for selecting displayed objects without manual input. A display presents a plurality of selectable icons and an animated visual cue associated with at least one icon. An eye-tracking sensor determines a user’s line of sight relative to the display. A controller monitors gaze movement and compares the detected line of sight with movement of the animated visual cue. When the user’s gaze follows the animated visual cue according to a predetermined correlation criterion, the controller selects the associated icon and initiates a corresponding command. The animated visual cue may include a moving image, trajectory, oscillation, or other time-varying visual pattern, thereby reducing inadvertent selections caused by momentary fixation and enabling gaze-based activation in hands-free computing environments.
counterfactuals.label: cf_1

counterfactuals.prompt: Generate a formal “present invention” summary describing a medical device with a display, gaze detector, animation icon, determination unit, and output unit for confirming intentional gaze selection.
counterfactuals.output:
The present invention relates to a medical device configured to receive and confirm an intentional gaze-based selection by a user. The medical device includes a display unit, a gaze detection unit, a determination unit, and an output unit.

The display unit is configured to display one or more selectable items and an animation icon associated with at least one of the selectable items. The gaze detection unit is configured to detect a gaze position, gaze direction, or gaze dwell state of the user with respect to the display unit. The animation icon is configured to change in appearance over time when the user’s gaze is detected within a predetermined region associated with the selectable item, thereby providing a visual indication that a gaze selection operation is in progress.

The determination unit is configured to determine whether the user’s gaze indicates an intentional selection of the selectable item based on gaze detection information obtained by the gaze detection unit and a state or progression of the animation icon. In one embodiment, the determination unit determines that the selection is intentional when the detected gaze remains within the predetermined region for at least a prescribed period, or until the animation icon reaches a predetermined completion state.

The output unit is configured to output a confirmation signal, control signal, notification, or command corresponding to the selected item when the determination unit determines that the user has intentionally selected the item. Accordingly, the medical device can reduce erroneous operation caused by accidental gaze contact and can improve safety and operability in a medical environment by confirming user intent through a gaze-based interaction accompanied by animation feedback.
counterfactuals.label: cf_2

counterfactuals.prompt: Describe an invention for reducing user burden in gaze-based UI operation, where an animated icon is selected only if the detected eye movement follows the icon’s animation.
counterfactuals.output:
An invention can reduce user burden in gaze-based user interface operation by making selection depend not merely on where the user is looking, but on whether the user’s eye movement intentionally follows a moving or animated target.

In one implementation, a display presents one or more selectable icons, buttons, or menu items. At least one icon is animated, for example by moving, oscillating, rotating, expanding and contracting, or following a predefined path. An eye-tracking device detects the user’s gaze position over time and generates eye-movement data. A controller compares the detected eye movement with the animation pattern of the icon.

The icon is selected only when the detected gaze movement corresponds to the icon’s animation within a predetermined tolerance. For example, if an icon moves in a small circular path, the system determines whether the user’s gaze also follows a similar circular path at approximately the same timing, phase, direction, or speed. If the gaze merely rests on the icon, briefly passes over it, or does not track the animated motion, the system does not activate the icon.

This reduces accidental selections caused by ordinary looking, scanning, or fixation. It also avoids requiring the user to dwell on an object for a long time, blink deliberately, or perform a separate manual confirmation. Because the user can confirm intent simply by visually following the animated icon, the interface becomes less tiring and more reliable, especially in hands-free environments such as AR/VR systems, assistive devices, vehicle interfaces, medical displays, or wearable computers.

The system may include:

- a display unit configured to present an animated selectable object;
- an eye-tracking unit configured to detect gaze direction or gaze position over time;
- a motion-correlation unit configured to compare the detected eye movement with the animation of the selectable object; and
- a selection controller configured to select or execute the object only when the correlation satisfies a threshold condition.

The animation may be assigned uniquely to different icons so that, when multiple icons are displayed, the system can determine which icon the user intended to select by identifying which animation pattern best matches the user’s gaze trajectory. The threshold may be adjusted based on user calibration, eye-tracking accuracy, icon size, display distance, or user ability.

In short, the invention provides a gaze-based selection technique in which an animated icon functions as an intentional visual “gesture target,” and selection occurs only when the user’s gaze tracks the icon’s movement, thereby lowering cognitive and physical burden while suppressing unintended activation.
counterfactuals.label: cf_4

counterfactuals.prompt: Create a Japanese patent translation-style abstract about a line-of-sight operation apparatus, method, and medical device using gaze tracking and animated icons to determine user selection.
counterfactuals.output:
【要約】  
【課題】使用者の視線に基づく操作において、意図しない選択を抑制しつつ、直感的かつ確実な入力を可能にする視線操作装置、視線操作方法、および医療機器を提供する。  

【解決手段】視線操作装置は、表示部と、使用者の視線位置を検出する視線検出部と、表示部に複数の操作対象アイコンを表示させる表示制御部と、検出された視線位置に基づいて操作対象アイコンのいずれかに対する注視状態を判定する判定部と、判定結果に基づいて使用者による選択操作を確定する制御部とを備える。表示制御部は、操作対象アイコンの少なくとも一部を、時間的に変化するアニメーションアイコンとして表示し、判定部は、視線位置がアニメーションアイコンの表示領域またはその変化に対応する所定領域に所定条件で追従または滞留した場合に、当該アニメーションアイコンが選択されたと判定する。これにより、単なる一時的な視線通過や誤注視による誤操作を低減できる。  

本視線操作装置は、内視鏡装置、手術支援装置、画像診断装置、患者モニタ装置等の医療機器に適用可能であり、使用者が手を用いずに機能選択、表示切替、設定変更、または処置具制御を行うことを可能にする。
